title: Ratio and sharing in a ratio
summary: Use two-colour bars to see what 2 : 3 means, simplify ratios, and share an amount in a given ratio.
guide: A {{term:ratio}} compares two amounts. 2 : 3 ("2 to 3") means for every 2 of the first, there are 3 of the second.
On the bar, shaded parts are the first thing and white parts are the second. A ratio of 2 : 3 is 2 shaded parts and 3 white parts, 5 parts altogether.
Careful: "2 to 3" is not "2 out of 3". In the ratio 2 : 3, the first thing is {{frac:2/5}} of the whole, not {{frac:2/3}}.
Equivalent ratios work like equivalent fractions: multiply or divide both numbers by the same number.

build-ratio.title: Squash, 2 : 3
build-ratio.prompt: Maryam is making squash: the ratio of cordial to water is 2 : 3. That's 2 cups of cordial for every 3 cups of water. Use + and − to get the right number of parts on the bar. Then shade the cordial parts; the white parts are water.
build-ratio.hint: Each cup is one part. How many cups altogether? Make the bar that many parts.
build-ratio.success: Well done! 2 parts cordial and 3 parts water: 5 parts altogether. The cordial is {{frac:2/5}} of the drink.
build-ratio.why: Reza says "a ratio of 2 : 3 means the cordial is {{frac:2/3}} of the drink". Is he right? Explain with the bar.
build-ratio.model: No. {{frac:2/3}} means "2 out of 3", but the ratio 2 : 3 compares cordial with water, not with the whole drink. The drink is 2 + 3 = 5 parts, so the cordial is {{frac:2/5}} and the water is {{frac:3/5}}. With 4 cups of cordial and 6 of water it tastes the same, because 4 : 6 is equivalent to 2 : 3.

feedback.too-big: Too much cordial! With only 3 parts there is no room for 3 cups of water. How many parts do 2 cups of cordial and 3 cups of water make?
feedback.too-small: Not enough cordial. For every 2 parts of cordial there should be only 3 parts of water.
feedback.empty: First get the right number of parts, then shade the cordial.

simplify-ratio.title: Simplify 6 : 9
simplify-ratio.prompt: Zahra has 6 red beads (shaded) and 9 blue beads (white). The ratio of red to blue is 6 : 9. 6 : 9 = 2 : what? Predict first. Then use − to put the beads into bigger groups until there are 5 groups.
simplify-ratio.hint: With 5 groups, how many groups are red and how many are blue?
simplify-ratio.success: Correct! 6 : 9 = 2 : 3: every 3 beads made one group.
simplify-ratio.why: Hassan says "6 : 9 = 2 : 5, because I took 4 off both". Why is that wrong?
simplify-ratio.model: For equivalent ratios we multiply or divide both numbers by the same number; we don't subtract. 6 and 9 are both divisible by 3: 6 ÷ 3 = 2 and 9 ÷ 3 = 3. On the bar, every 3 beads became one group: 2 red groups and 3 blue groups. Taking 4 off both leaves 2 red and 5 blue, which has more blue for each red than before, so it isn't the same ratio.

feedback.additive: You took 4 off both numbers. For a ratio you divide: what did 6 get divided by to make 2? Divide 9 by the same number.
feedback.unchanged: 9 is all the blue beads. When 6 simplifies to 2, the 9 has to simplify too.
feedback.too-big: Too big. 6 was divided by 3 to make 2. Divide 9 by 3 as well.

ratio-to-fraction.title: From ratio to fraction
ratio-to-fraction.prompt: In a class the ratio of boys to girls is 3 : 4. What fraction of the class are girls? Predict first. Then build the bar and shade the girls' parts. Type the answer as a fraction.
ratio-to-fraction.hint: For every 3 boys there are 4 girls. How many children are in one full group?
ratio-to-fraction.success: Well done! In every 7 children, 4 are girls: the girls are {{frac:4/7}} of the class and the boys {{frac:3/7}}.
ratio-to-fraction.why: If there are 28 children in the class, how many are girls? Explain with the 7-part bar.
ratio-to-fraction.model: The bar has 7 parts and 28 children share into 7 parts: each part is 28 ÷ 7 = 4 children. The girls are 4 parts, so 4 × 4 = 16 girls. That is, {{frac:4/7}} of 28 is 16. The boys are 3 parts, 12 children, and 12 : 16 is the same as 3 : 4.

feedback.ratio-as-fraction: That fraction compares boys and girls with each other. But the question is what fraction of the whole class are girls. How many parts is the whole class?
feedback.boys: {{frac:3/7}} is the fraction of boys. What fraction are girls?
feedback.too-big: Too big. The denominator must be all the children: 3 boys and 4 girls.
feedback.too-small: Too small. How many girls are in each group?
feedback.empty: Type the fraction: numerator and denominator.

share-in-ratio.title: Share 28 walnuts in the ratio 3 : 4
share-in-ratio.prompt: Ali and Sara share 28 walnuts in the ratio 3 : 4. The 3 blue parts are Ali's share. Shade Sara's parts. First predict: how many walnuts does Sara get?
share-in-ratio.hint: The bar has 7 parts altogether and shows 28 walnuts. How many walnuts in each part?
share-in-ratio.success: Correct! Each part is 28 ÷ 7 = 4 walnuts. Sara has 4 parts: 4 × 4 = 16 walnuts. Ali gets 12, and 12 + 16 = 28.
share-in-ratio.why: Ahmad divided 28 by 4 and said Sara's share is 7. Why do we divide by 7?
share-in-ratio.model: The ratio 3 : 4 means the walnuts are split into 3 + 4 = 7 equal parts. So first divide 28 by 7 to find one part: 4 walnuts. Sara gets 4 parts: 16 walnuts. Dividing 28 by 4 treats the walnuts as only 4 parts and forgets Ali's share. Check: 12 + 16 = 28.

feedback.other-share: 12 is Ali's share (3 parts). Sara's share is 4 parts.
feedback.divided-by-part: You divided 28 by 4. But the walnuts are split into 3 + 4 = 7 equal parts.
feedback.one-part: 4 walnuts is just one part. Sara gets 4 parts.
feedback.halved: You split them half and half. But the ratio is 3 : 4, not 1 : 1: Sara gets more than Ali.
feedback.too-big: Too many. Ali gets 3 parts too; leave some for him.
feedback.too-small: Too few. Sara gets 4 of the 7 parts, more than half.
feedback.empty: Type a number: how many walnuts does Sara get?
